summary: Prefetch cache invalidation after regional failover caused sustained p99 inference latency spike
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC ParcelLeaf reported sustained p99 token latency increases (2.4s -> 9.8s) for generation requests after an automatic regional failover. Impact: customer production traffic experienced elevated tail latency and several user-facing timeouts; revenue-impacting. Timeline: 09:08 UTC internal health checks detected degraded node pool in us-east-1 and a failover policy moved ~18% of live sessions to us-west-2 by 09:10 UTC. By 09:12 customers reported p95/p99 regressions and streaming stalls. Steps to reproduce: 1) Under heavy request mix that includes multi-model routing, trigger controlled node drain in primary region (simulate degraded host). 2) Observe routing change and measure per-request latency distribution while performing warm vs cold requests. 3) Note KV/prefix cache fill rates and disk IO during first 10 minutes after failover. Observed metrics/logs: - p50 ~ unchanged, p95 up 2.2x, p99 up ~4x for affected routes. - serving-runtime metrics show cache-miss rate jumped from 6% to 84% immediately after failover. - kv-cache prefetch queue length spiked and worker CPU on us-west-2 increased by 70%. - edge-proxy connection reuse dropped (connections per instance decreased ~60%) causing more TLS/TCP setup for new backend connections. - No errors in model binary loads; model latency (once cache warm) returns to baseline. Initial hypothesis: The routing failover sent large number of requests to nodes that did not share warmed KV/prefix caches; the runtime attempted aggressive prefetching to rebuild local caches which caused high IO and request queuing, producing tail latency. Additionally, connection reuse breakage across the egress/proxy layer amplified overhead for each new request. Investigation notes: - Correlated cache-miss spikes with routing change event ID route-flip-2026-03-10-0910. - Dashboard: /dashboards/latency/route-flip-2026-03-10 shows bloom in prefetch activity. - Cache TTL and replication settings: discovered that prefix cache replication was disabled for dedicated customers to avoid cross-tenant data transfer; this allowed cold nodes to require full prefetch after any affinity flip. - Reproduction in staging: reproduced by disabling affinity for 60s and observed identical p99 spike pattern. Temporary mitigation deployed: 1) Re-enabled affinity stickiness for the customer's routing policy to avoid immediate traffic redistribution while caches warm (09:38 UTC). 2) Throttled prefetch concurrency to limit IO pressure on newly promoted nodes (09:45 UTC). 3) Enabled connection pool fallback to maintain existing upstream connections when possible. Result: p99 recovered to within 1.1x baseline by 10:05 UTC. Root cause: regional failover caused large-scale cold-starts of local prefix/KV caches combined with aggressive prefetching and reduced connection reuse. Long-term fix plan: - Short term (this week): introduce a staged traffic drain for failovers (gradual ramp) to give caches time to warm; adjust default prefetch concurrency settings for dedicated customers. - Medium term (1-2 sprints): implement cross-region cache metadata replication (non-sensitive keys) to allow quick warm-up without transferring sensitive prefixes; add configurable sticky-affinity window for dedicated customers. - Postmortem owner: SRE + Serving Runtime team. Follow-ups: update runbook, publish postmortem on Confluence, notify affected customers of remediation.
